title: Do so; such
subtitle: seems likely to do so / such a scheme
summary: Replace a repeated verb phrase with do so, and refer back to a kind of thing with such (a / an).

lesson.heading: do so instead of a verb phrase
lesson.text: Do so (does so, did so, doing so, done so) replaces a whole verb phrase - the verb and everything needed to complete its meaning - when the context makes clear what we mean.

examples.text: She won in 2012 and seems likely to **do so** again this year.
Dr Lawson said, 'Sit down.' Katia **did so**, and explained her problem.
The climbers will try again today to reach the summit. Their chances of **doing so** are better than they were last week.
When he was asked to check the figures, he claimed that he had already **done so**.

lesson.heading: How formal is do so?
lesson.text: Do so belongs to formal spoken and written English. In informal English we can use do it or do that instead, and after a modal or a perfect tense we can use do on its own.

examples.text: Mrs Chen waved as she walked past. She **does so / it / that** every morning.
Ricardo told me to put in a new battery. I **did so / it / that**, but the radio still doesn't work.
*A:* Will this program work on your computer? *B:* It **should do**.
I told you that I'd finish the work by today, and I **have done**.

lesson.heading: Actions, but not states or habits

left.label: Actions - do so is fine
examples: 65% of the members voted for Katie Brown this time, whereas 84% **did so** last year.
Kenyon confessed to the murder, although he only **did so** after a number of witnesses had identified him as the killer.
I gave her the medicine, and I take full responsibility for **doing so**.

right.label: States and habitual actions - do alone
examples: Lars doesn't like Facebook but Emma **does**.
He earned a lot more than I **did**.
I don't have time to go swimming every day, but I usually **do**.

lesson.heading: such + noun = 'of this kind'
lesson.text: Such refers back to something already mentioned and means 'of this / that kind'. Use such + noun with uncountable and plural nouns, and such + a / an + noun with singular countable nouns. This use is mainly formal.

examples.text: The students refer to teachers by their first names and will often criticise them for badly prepared lessons. **Such behaviour** is unacceptable in most schools.
When asked about rumours that the company is preparing to lose more than 200 jobs, a spokeswoman said: 'I know of **no such plans**.'
They needed someone who was both an excellent administrator and manager. **Such a person** was not easy to find.
We allow both men and women to have time off work to look after children. We were the first department to introduce **such a scheme**.

lesson.heading: Formal such and its everyday equivalents
rows: **Such behaviour** is unacceptable in most schools.
Behaviour like this is unacceptable in most schools.
I know of no plans of this kind.
**Such a person** was not easy to find.
A person like this was not easy to find.
Is there really a computer in **such a device**?
Is there really a computer in a device like this?
She called on the government to put more money into **such research**.
... to put more money into research of this kind.

lesson.text: Before you write do so, check the verb: if it describes a state (like, enjoy, smell) or a habit, use do, does or did on its own.

exercises.prompt: If you have not already handed in the form, then please ___ without delay.
exercises.explanation: Do so replaces 'hand in the form' - typical of formal written instructions.

exercises.prompt: My French hosts gave me snails to eat, but I ___ very reluctantly.
exercises.explanation: Did so replaces 'ate them' - a single action, so do so works.

exercises.prompt: He jumped down from the window, but in ___ twisted his ankle.
exercises.explanation: After a preposition (in) we need the -ing form doing so.

exercises.prompt: Olav drives much faster than you ___.
exercises.explanation: Driving here is a habitual action, and we avoid do so with habits.

exercises.statement: I thought Julie was joking when she said these apples smell like oranges. But they do so!
exercises.explanation: But they do! Smell describes a state here, so do so is not used.

exercises.prompt: All EU countries agreed to implement the new regulations on recycling plastic, but so far only Finland and Austria ___.
exercises.explanation: Have done so replaces 'have implemented the new regulations'.

exercises.prompt: Join the two ideas: She was asked to teach more classes. She was happy to teach more classes.
exercises.answer: She was asked to teach more classes, and was happy to do so.
exercises.explanation: Do so avoids repeating the verb phrase 'teach more classes'.

exercises.prompt: In each sentence, is the missing form do so or do / does / did on its own?

items.text: Anyone crossing the railway ... at their own risk.
She pointed to the old box, her hand shaking as she ... .
The water freezes in the cracks in rocks, and as it ... it expands.
I know that many people don't enjoy Felipe's blog, but I ... .
As a rule Leyla wins at tennis, and she gets upset if I ... .
*A:* These apples smell like oranges. *B:* You're right - they ... !

exercises.prompt: Manufacturers often claim that their washing machines have built-in computers, but is there really a computer in ___?
exercises.explanation: Device is a singular countable noun, so we use such + a + noun.

exercises.prompt: Building a new power station would undoubtedly create new jobs, but has the environmental impact of ___ been considered fully?
exercises.explanation: Such a project = a project of this kind.

exercises.prompt: The earthquake demolished thousands of buildings. The country has rarely seen ___ before.
exercises.explanation: Destruction is uncountable, so such is used without a / an.

exercises.prompt: Match each formal sentence with its more informal version.

pairs.left: Such behaviour is unacceptable in most schools.
pairs.right: Behaviour like this is unacceptable in most schools.

pairs.left: I know of no such plans.
pairs.right: I know of no plans of this kind.

pairs.left: Such a person was not easy to find.
pairs.right: A person like this was not easy to find.

pairs.left: Is there really a computer in such a device?
pairs.right: Is there really a computer in a device like this?

pairs.left: She called on the government to put more money into such research.
pairs.right: She called on the government to put more money into research of this kind.
